content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: move 2 cross-skilled agents from general to payments (09:00-14:00) and switch on IVR callback for payments (09:00-15:00), at no extra cost.","why":"This morning's problem is staffing, not demand. Payments had 7 flu sick calls against a usual 2 per day, leaving 13 agents on the phones against 18 planned. Volume is only 5.4% over forecast, and handle time is close to plan. P1 is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target over the 09:00-15:00 window, at a predicted 80.1% overall. Abandons are predicted to fall to 5.1%, against 78.3% service level and 5.5% abandons if we do nothing. It costs INR 0 and breaks no policy. General is not hurt: it actually edges up from 89.5% to 89.9%.","trade_offs":["Payments itself stays weak at 72.8% under P1. The plan meets target only on the combined figure, so payments callers still wait longer than standard.","The 80.1% prediction gives almost no margin over the 80% target. If more absences come in or volume rises further, P1 could fall short.","P2 costs INR 1,056 and lifts payments to 77.7% (83.1% overall, 4.1% abandons). It relies on deflecting 20% of payment status calls to chat and on moving 3 agents out of general until 11:00.","P3 costs INR 4,500 and adds overtime, reaching 84.1% overall with payments at 78.9%. P4 costs INR 8,280, takes no one from general, and gives the strongest result: 89.4% overall, payments 86.1%, 2.4% abandons."],"watch":"Watch payments service level and abandons after 09:00, and any further sick calls. If payments is not recovering toward the low 70s by mid-morning, or the overall figure dips below 80%, move to P2. P2 is the cheap step up, and overtime (P3/P4) is the fallback. No escalation to the duty manager is needed."}
